The vehicles were kept in storage until January 7, 2020, when it was announced that they were being put into use. It is unclear when they were delivered to Papua New Guinea.

column8: Chinese Government provides RMB 10.3 million grant for provision of supplies and equipment to support the 11th ASEM Summit
column9: On January 5, 2016, Chinese Government and the Government of Mongolia signed letters of exchange, which committed RMB 10,395100 of grant funding for the provision of furniture and  audio-visual equipment — including simultaneous interpretation equipment, fire-fighting equipment, police equipment, large conference tables, sofas, and podiums — to support the 11th ASEM Summit in July 2016. The grant agreement was signed by the Minister of Commerce of the People's Republic of China (Gao Huchen). China Civil Engineering Construction Group Co., Ltd. and Jiangsu Sainty Co., Ltd.  were the contractors responsible for implementation. One batch of supplies and equipment arrived by plane on April 29, 2016. Another batch arrived by train on June 18, 2016.  All supplies were handed over by July 21, 2016.

column8: China donates 700 milion Comorian Francs worth stability maintenance supplies to Comoros Ministry of Defense
column9: On June 9th, 2018, the Ambassador of China in Comoros handed over a donation of stability maintenance supplies for the Comoros Ministry of Defense to improve policing, anti-terrorism, stability, and security enforcement apparatus (援科摩罗维稳物资项目交接仪式在莫罗尼举行). The materials include 15 buses, 30 pickup trucks, 60 desktop computers, 60 black-and-white laser printers, 5 black-and-white copiers, power supplies, and various other consumables. At the ceremony, both Comorian and Chinese officials gave speeches praising defense cooperation. He Yanjun, the Chinese ambassador to Comoros, and Joseph Mohamed Ali, the Comoros Minister of Defense, signed the handover certificate on behalf of the two governments.  Comorian news outlet Al-Watwan reports that the total value of the donation is estimated to be roughly 700 million Comorian Francs (Coopération militaire sino-comorienne : La Chine remet un don de matériels de sécurité à la gendarmerie nationale).

column8: China provides 10 million RMB medical equipment donation for Parakou Army Instruction Hospital  (linked to #34144, #72795)
column9: The Chinese-funded Parakou Army Instruction Hospital was inaugurated on February 13, 2011, and started its clinical activities on October 4, 2011 after a phase 1 construction costing 6 billion CFAF (see Project #34144). In order to improve the functioning of the said hospital and to improve its equipment, the Chinese government had offered an additional 11.5 million yuan or 920 million CFA francs for the second phase in April 2013, which allowed the construction of the water tower, the canteen, housing for duty guards, etc (see Project #72795). The Parakou Military Instruction Hospital was then officially handed over on Thursday, April 3, 2014. After this second phase, the government decides to provide medical equipment in the form of a donation for an amount of 10 million yuan or 800 million CFA francs to the hospital in Parakou. This equipment will help improve the services of the said hospital for the benefit of the populations of Parakou and the surrounding area._x000D_ _x000D_ Located in the Okédama district on the edge of the interstate road, it is a set of four groups of buildings on two levels arranged in a "U" and connected to each other. This set is made up of three blocks: an administrative block comprising the management and its components and an amphitheater with 256 seats; a medical-technical unit with many units: medicine, surgery, maternity, odontostomatology, emergencies, radiology services, biomedical analysis laboratory, a complex of three operating theaters, a research and fight center against malaria and a laundry room; a technical unit comprising a generator with a power of 550 KVA, a water tower with a capacity of 50,000 liters, a canteen with 100 places, a guardhouse building, a mortuary and an electrical technical room and incinerator.

column8: Chinese Government donates 2 luxury vehicles for Victory Day Parade
column9: On April 8, 2015, the Chinese Government donated two FAW HongQi L5 (“Red Banner”) grand vehicles to the Government of Belarus ahead of its Minsk Victory Day Parade. The vehicles reportedly have an estimated value of RMB 5 million each and they were financed with a military grant from the Chinese Government.

column8: China Grants 19 Vehicles Worth USD $1.6M to Dominica for Hurricane Maria Relief (Linked to ID#55319 and ID#55325)
column9: China donated 19 military vehicles, which included a fire truck, ambulances, cargo trucks and so on, as well as materials for these vehicles and the equipment for repairing these materials at a sum of $1.6 million. The hand over ceremony was held at the Windsor Park Stadium on April 10th, 2018. This logistic material aid was expected to enhance Dominica's capacity in areas of recovery, disaster reduction and maintaining stability in a medical emergency.

column8: Ministry of National Defense of the People's Republic of China Donates Hospital and Medical Equipment to Costa Rica's Ministry of Public Security
column9: On December 26, 2011, the donation of hospital and medical equipment by the Ministry of National Defense of the People's Republic of China to the Health Area of the Ministry of Public Security of Costa Rica was approved. The donation was worth 1.4 Million USD. The project was executed between 2011 and 2012, with an exchange of letters (canje de notas) related to the project's execution taking place July 31, 2012.   The purpose of the project was to improve the quality of health attention given to officials in Costa Rica's Ministry of Public Security. The name of the project according to Costa Rica's Ministry of Planning and Economic Policy is "Donación Equipo Médico y Hospitalario."  The project may have been funded through a Free Logistics Assistance Agreement (Acuerdo sobre la Asistencia Logística Gratuita), also signed December 26, 2011 by the Ministry of Public Security of Costa Rica and the Ministry of National Defense of China, which is listed in the "project monitoring" section of the database entry about the donation.

column8: Chinese Ministry of Public Security grants aid worth $640,640 to Tajik Ministry of Internal Affairs
column9: In 2002, the Chinese Ministry of Public Security and the Tajik Ministry of Internal Affairs (also known as the Ministry of the Interior) signed an agreement on the fight against terrorism, extremism and separatism, which included the provision of no-strings aid to Tajikistan. The aid was handed over on March 11, 2003. The aid consisted of twenty patrol cars (Radio Free Europe suggests it was 50 vehicles), special equipment, computers, laser printers, uniforms and footwear for the ministry's special subdivisions, special crime detection equipment, communication devices, night vision binoculars, cameras, metal detectors, shields, and helmets, among other goods. Material for bomb defusal was also included. _x000D_ _x000D_ Media sources indicate that the value of the aid was $700,000. However, according to the Flat Export from Tajikistan AIMS as of May 2018, the Chinese government funded "Policemen facilities" (AIMS project ID TJK/042056) worth $483,600. Additionally, there was an additional contribution of $157,040 USD for "Different kind of equipment" (AIMS project ID TJK/042058). Together, these two donations totaled $640,640, therefore it seems they are referencing this same project, even though transaction amounts differ slightly, so the transaction amount was coded as $640,640 USD to reflect official source information.

column8: Chinese Government provides $630,000 grant to provide equipment to military hospital in Belarus
column9: On September 28, 2003, the Main Military Clinical Hospital of the Ministry of Defense of Belarus received modern medical equipment worth $630,000 as part of a humanitarian aid program from the People's Republic of China. The Belarusian Defense minister, the Chinese ambassador extraordinary and plenipotentiary to Belarus, Yu Zhenqi, and other officials attended a ceremony dedicated to the signing of an agreement on its transfer. The Chinese Ministry of National Defense had previously to provide a grant worth RMB to million Military Hospital in April 2002.

column8: Chinese government donates equipment for Pekoa Airport to Vanuatu
column9: In 2005, the Chinese government donated $700,000 worth of equipment to the Peoka Aiport in Vanuatu, located in the city of Luganville on Espiritu Santo, the largest island of Vanuatu. According to page AIII-vi of "The Dragon Looks South," the equipment included x-ray machines to improve security screening, a baggage conveyor, and fire equipment. The exact start and end dates are unclear.

column8: Chinese Ministry of Defense funds 10 million RMB of mobile field hospital grant worth 18 million RMB through Free Military Assistance Agreement (Linked to Record ID#88255)
column9: On May 9, 2012, the Ministries of Defense of Ecuador and China signed a protocol agreement, which agreed to grant a mobile field hospital, consisting of vehicles and other equipment, worth 18 million RMB. The field hospital was to be used in Loja by the Motorized Infantry Brigade, part of Ecuador's Armed Forces (FF.AA). Its was to be used for medical emergencies and rescue operations during natural disasters.  This mobile field hospital was co-financed by the China's Ministry of Defense (captured in this project, 10 million RMB out of 18 million RMB) and the People's Liberation Army (captured in #88255, 8 million RMB out of 18 million RMB). Both the Ministry of Defense and the PLA funded the field hospital through a Free Military Assistance Agreement with Ecuador.   The Free Military Assistance Agreement between China's Ministry of Defense and Ecuador's Ministry of Defense was signed December 27, 2011, and provided a 10 million RMB grant captured in this project. The entire amount was used for the field hospital project. The Free Military Assistance Agreement between the PLA and the Armed Forces of Ecuador was signed November 12, 2010, and provided an 8 million RMB grant, which is captured in Record ID#. The entire amount was used to fund the field hospital project as well.  More specifically, the grant contained one of each of the following vehicles: ambulance, surgery vehicle, clinical laboratory vehicle, x-ray and type B ultrasound vehicle, sterilization/pharmacy/storage vehicle, restaurant vehicle, vehicle for medical oxygen preparation, shower vehicle, water purifying vehicle, and support vehicle. It also included one transition tent; four tents with a bed and equipment for triage, ICU, and care; and spare parts for two years of use.  The handover ceremony took place in Loja on July 19, 2013.

column8: China grants Kyrgyz Republic 5 million RMB for food and other materials

column8: China donates second batch of riot equipment worth SBD 12 million (linked to project ID#93528)
column9: On December 23, 2021, the Chinese Government agreed to donate riot equipment (captured via Project ID #93528) and provide six police liaison officers (captured via Project ID #93529) to equip and train the Royal Solomon Islands Police Force (RSIPF). The riot gear includes shields, helmets, batons, and other non-lethal equipment. On December 29, 2021, the Chinese Ambassador officially handed over a batch of riot equipment as it arrived at the Henderson International Airport. This was part of a larger donation, and a second batch of riot gear worth USD 12 million arrived on February  24, 2022. The donation was received in a handover ceremony at Rove Police Headquarters. Nine Chinese police liaison officers arrived in the Solomon Islands in March 2022 to train RSIPF officers in anti-riot strategies.   In 2019, Solomon Islands' Prime Minister Manasseh Sogavare withdrew recognition of the Republic of China (Taiwan) and established diplomatic relations with the People's Republic of China (PRC). Malaita Province, an island struggling with unemployment and poverty, maintained informal ties with Taiwan. The premier of Malaita Province, Daniel Suidani, even held an independence referendum in 2020, which the national government dismissed as illegitimate. At the same time, Chinese businesses across the Solomon Islands were accused of giving jobs to foreigners instead of locals.  Between November 24 and 27, 2021, a series of protests in the Solomon Islands against relations with the PRC turned violent. Protesters attempted to storm Parliament and depose Prime Minister Sogavare. Businesses, mainly in Honiara's Chinatown district, were burnt and looted. A police station was set on fire. The government responded by deploying the police in which they used tear gas. Australia deployed the Australian Federal Police and Defence Force. Papua New Guinea and Fiji dispatched peacekeepers while New Zealand deployed police and troops.

column8: Chinese Government provides PGK 1.5 million grant for Taurama Military Hospital Upgrading Project (Linked to Project ID#42128)

column8: Chinese Ministry of Defense donates medical equipment worth 755,000 euros to the Serbian military on July 2020

column8: Chinese Ministry of Public Security provides RMB 4.5 million grant for police materials

column8: China Poly Group donated 96 machines to Uganda Police Uniform Factory
column9: In 2014, the Chinese company, China Poly Technologies Inc, donated 96 machines worth $800,000 to the Ugandan Police garment factory and send technicians to train local employees. The grant also included a 16-seater bus, a boxing ring, boxing gloves, punchbags, and fighting gear for the Vanuatu Police Force. (Linked to Record ID #104567).

column8: Chinese pathologist team provides technical assistance in autopsies to Samoan Ministry of Health
column9: On April 29, 2021, a team of 8 Chinese forensic pathologists arrived in Apia Samoa to assist in the post-mortem examination of a backlog of 13 bodies that have been stored in the morgue for almost 1 year awaiting autopsies. The Chinese government provided the equipment for the post-mortem examination and also covered all the expenses including the autopsy, traveling, and accommodation of the Chinese forensic pathologist team, costing more than 500,000 Tala.    At the additional request of the Samoan government, the Chinese forensic pathologist team also conducted 3 more autopsies of current cases. The team also conducted two forensic technical training lectures at the invitation of the Samoa Police, including the crime scene investigation and the fingerprint application.

column8: ZTE donation of radio equipment to Mauritius Police Force
column9: ZTE Corporation China donated two B.T.S. radio sets (Model ZXC10) worth Rs. 4,960,000 to the Mauritius Police Department, specifically the Communications Branch.  The date of donation is listed as April 5 2012.

column8: Chinese Government grants RMB 700,000 for the provision of police equipment
column9: On November 26, 2004, Chinese Government signed an RMB 700,000 grant for the provision of police equipment. Under the agreement between the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Republic of Uzbekistan and the Ministry of Public Security of the People’s Republic of China, the Chinese government granted 700,000 RMB to the Ministry of the Internal Affairs of the Republic of Uzbekistan.

column8: China grants $211,781 USD to Liberia National Police for Ebola response (Linked to Record ID#41547, #45060)
column9: In 2014, China committed to various sectors of the Government of Liberia over 3 million dollars to fight Ebola. During the signing ceremony, the PRC Government is providing US$1 million cash to the Liberian Government (see #41547); US $2 million to the World Food Programme (WFP) (see #45060), and US $211,781 logistical support to the LNP. This project captures the donation to the LNP, which includes vehicles, motorcycles, communication equipment, among others.  Other Ebola-related assistance provided by the Chinese Government in 2014 is captured in umbrella Record ID#60642.

column8: China's Ministry of National Defense donates medical equipment to Sri Lanka's Ministry of Defence
column9: On May 12, 2020, China's Ministry of National Defense donated 70,000 disposable medical masks, 9,000 surgical masks, 9,000 medical surgical masks (KN95), 6,300 medical protective goggles, 4,500 disposable medical protective screens (face shields), 4,500 disposable one-piece medical protective suits, 4,500 disposable medical isolation (170) gowns, 9,000 pairs of disposable medical boot covers, 80 disposable medical gloves, 160 disposable nitrile gloves 50-packets,  30 infusion pumps, two 16-litere Knapsack disinfectant sprayers (16L), 70 frontal temperature gun CK - T1501 (IR thermometers) and two Thermal Imaging Smart Helmet (N901) (infrared image temperature observing helmets) to Sri Lanka's Defence Ministry. A People’s Liberation Army-Air Force Y-20 delivered the donation.

column8: China provides $150,000 worth of office and communication equipment to CTSAMM, South Sudan (linked to #53322)
column9: On April 28th, 2016, the Chinese government provided $150,000 worth of office and communication equipment to the South Sudan Ceasefire and Transitional Security Arrangements Monitoring Mechanism (CTSAMM) at the CTSAMM headquarters in Juba. This grant is intended to ease the peace negotiation process in South Sudan._x000D_ _x000D_ This project is one of the two grants to CTSAMM made in the same event. The other one is a $550,000 cash grant, which is reported in #53322.

column8: Chinese Government grants 131,652 euros to Albania for Non-traditional Security Threats Seminar
column9: In 2017, the Chinese Government granted 131,652 euros for a Seminar on Non-traditional Security Threats for Albania in Hangzhou, China. Seminar participants were from the State Police & Ministry of Interior. This project started on May 4, 2017 and reached completion on May 24, 2017. The seminar was to teach the State Police & Ministry of Interior on how to handle security threats, organized crime, terrorism, and trafficking.

column8: China offers technical assistance to Kyrgyz's Border Service
column9: In 2017, China's Ministry of Public Security agreed to provide technical assistance worth 1 million yuan to the Kyrgyz Border Service. This agreement was signed in context of strengthening cooperation between the two countries in the fields of counter-terrorism and personnel support. China additionally proposed training cooperation between Chinese and Kyrgyz personnel.

column8: China Commits to Give Uniforms worth US$150,000 to Uzbekistan's Police
column9: In February 2015, the Ministry of Public Security of China signed an agreement to provide uniforms (summer and winter clothing) to Uzbekistan's Ministry of Internal Affairs' policemen for a total amount of USD$150,000.

column8: Chinese Government donates communications equipment worth $75,000 to Timor-Leste’s Ministry of Home Affairs
column9: On September 8, 2005, the handover ceremony for the Chinese donation of police supplies and communications equipment to Timor-Leste was held at the Ministry of Home Affairs (援助东帝汶内政部警用物资). Chinese Ambassador to Timor-Leste Chen Duqing and Minister of Home Affairs Rogerio Lobato [罗热里奥·洛巴托] handed over the police supplies (captured in #64675) and communications equipment from the Chinese Ministry of Public Security, and both signed the transfer certificate. According to Timor Leste's 2006-07 General Budget of the State, the funding for the communications equipment amounted to 75,000 USD.

column8: Chinese People's Liberation Army donates anti-epidemic materials in June 2020 to Zimbabwe National Defense Forces
column9: On June 4, 2020, anti-epidemic materials provided by the Chinese People's Liberation Army to the Zimbabwe National Defense Forces arrived at the Harareman Air Base in Zimbabwe. The materials included 62,000 masks, 19,000 pieces of personal protection equipment, and other critical medical supplies. China’s Ambassador to Zimbabwe, Guo Shaochun, the Minister of Defense and Veterans Affairs of Zimbabwe, and the Commander of the National Defense Forces attended the handover ceremony.

column8: Chinese Government provides fingerprint image-only matching lab worth USD $147,574.37 to Fiji police force
column9: In January of 2021, the Chinese Government donated a fingerprint image-only matching lab to the Fiji police. This donation is worth USD $147,574.37. The specific use of this donation is unspecified and requires more investigation.

column8: Chinese Government donates computers, printers, and rain coats to the Zambian Police Service
column9: In 2003, the Chinese Government donated 10 computers, 10 printers, and 1,000 rain coats worth more than $60,000 USD to the Zambian Police Service.

In June 2010, the China State Construction Engineering Corporation (CSCEC) reduced the amount owed by the Salvation Army of Barbados by 100,000 USD. _x000D_ _x000D_ Between February 2005 and November 2006, CSCEC constructed a new accommodation building and restaurant project for the charitable organization. The opening ceremony for the project took place in December 2006. The project cost a total of 350,000 USD, owed to the CSCEC, but the Salvation Army struggled to pay the full amount. In July 2010, the contractor decided to reduce the amount owed as a contribution to the charity. For forgiving the debt, the CSCEC was awarded the "Outstanding Contribution Award to Charity."

column7: Lesotho Ministry of Police and Public Safety
column8: China's Ministry of Public Security Donates 30 Motorbikes to Lesotho's Ministry of Police and Public Safety September 2020
column9: On September 10, 2020, the Chinese Ministry of Public Security donated 30 motorbikes to Lesotho's Ministry of Police and Public Safety. These bikes were estimated to be worth 2 million loti. They all had a logo that said "China Aid" on them. At the handover ceremony, Chinese Ambassador to Lesotho Lei Kezhong stated that the motorbikes were donated to strengthen safety and law enforcement in Lesotho.

column8: Chinese government donates CVE 15 million worth of forensic equipment to Cabo Verde Judicial Police, September 2023
column9: On September 6, 2023, the Chinese ambassador in Cabo Verde held a handover ceremony of a batch of forensic equipment for the Cabo Verde Judicial Police (Polícia Judiciária). This donation included computer equipment for the digital forensic laboratory that was worth CVE 15 million.

column8: The Chinese Consulate General in Kuching donates 380,000 masks to various sectors of the Sarawak government (linked to project ID #96940, #96941)
column9: In June 2021, the Chinese Consulate General in Kuching donated 380,000 masks to various sectors of the Sarawak government, including the Kuching Airport Immigration Bureau, Police Station, Fire and Rescue Bureau, charity organizations and other sectors of Sarawak. The staff of the Consulate General donated the masks directly.   This was part of a series of donations to various entities in Sarawak State, Malaysia, in June 2021. Other donations include 99,000 masks (30 boxes) to the Federation of Sarawak Chinese Associations (see project ID #96940) and a donation of 201,000 masks (67 boxes) to the Sarawak State Disaster Management Committee (see project ID #96941).

column8: Chinese Government donates 143,000 USD modern fingerprint and forensic science laboratory to Malawi Police Service
column9: On July 28, 2023, the Chinese Government provided a 143,000 USD fingerprint testing laboratory to the Malawi Police Service (MPS) in a handover ceremony in Lilongwe, Malawi. The donation will bridge the technological gap in Malawi’s police force.

column8: Unspecified Chinese Government Institution grants police supplies worth RMB 1 million to Madagascar
column9: In 2021, China and Madagascar signed a cooperation agreement for police supplies. On June 21, 2023, Zhang Wei, Charge d'Affaires of the Chinese Embassy in Madagascar and the Secretary-General of Madagascar's Ministry of Public Security signed a handover certificate for the donation of police supplies.  The equipment included including VPN servers, security gateways, network switches, laptops, uninterruptible power supplies, and other electronic equipment. This grant was to help Madagascar's government upgrade the police communication system and upgrade to the "I-24/7" communication system. The value of the equipment is RMB 1 million.  The equipment was expected to arrive May 3, 2023, in the port of Toamasina. It was handed over June 21, 2023. The donation is being implemented through the National Central Bureau of INTERPOL in Madagascar.  The Madagascar national police said the donation would allow them to detect suspicious persons entering Madagascar from other countries. It will Madagascar's INTERPOL office to communicate with other countries' INTERPOL offices and store data on suspicious persons entering and leaving the country.

column8: Chinese Embassy funds feasibility study for project strengthening ECU 911 through ETCA (linked to #35814)
column9: On August 12 and 24, 2015, the governments of China and Ecuador signed and countersigned Letters of Exchange committing 700,000 RMB (or  107,373 USD) to be used for a feasibility study for the "Equipment for the Strengthening of the Integrated Security Service ECU 911 in the Coastal and Rural Areas" project (Dotación de Equipamiento para el Fortalecimiento del Servicio Integrado de Seguridad ECU 911 en el Litoral y Áreas Rurales). The Chinese government agreed to send a team of experts to Ecuador in order to carry out the study.  The project was funded through the grant provided in an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA) singed on June 2, 2006 (see project #35814).  The executing agency was the Ecuador Ministry of Coordination for Internal and External Security (Ministerio de Coordinacion de Seguirdad Interna y Externa). The Chinese Embassy additionally helped with project implementation, and 100% of the funds have been disbursed.

column8: Chinese Government donates Digital Forensic Laboratory Equipment worth RMB 1 million to Seychelles Police Force, November 2023
column9: On November 13, 2023. the Chinese government handed over digital forensic laboratory equipment to the Seychelles police. The laboratory's major functions include data extraction, storage media back-up, quick data acquisition, data analysis and authentication, and data recovery.   The equipment is valued at RMB 1 million.

column8: China donated PHP 5M to the Philippines for troops injured in Marawi city [September 6th] (linked to #65137)
column9: On September 6, 2017, China donated a PHP 5 million check for injured soldiers from Marawi City. Chinese Ambassador to the Philippines Zhao Jianhua turned over the donation to Armed Forces of the Philippines chief of staff Gen in Camp Aguinaldo, Quezon City._x000D_ _x000D_ This project is linked to project #65137, a PHP 65 million donation for wounded troops made on September 13, 2017

column8: Beijing Municipal Government provides donation of 10,000 test kits and PPE to San José Municipal Government in November 2020
column9: On November 4, 2020, the Chinese Ambassador to Costa Rica handed over a donation from the Beijing Municipal Government to the Municipality of San José. The donation consisted of 10,000 PCR testing kits, as well as an unknown number of protective clothing, isolation glasses, surgical gloves, and thermometers.   The testing kits were to be delivered to the Costa Rican Social Security Fund (CCSS), which would in turn use them in clinics in the Central Canton of San José and mass testing in affected areas of the city. The PPE was to be used by front line workers collaborating with the municipal government.

column7: Sao Tome and Principe Ministry of Justice
column8: Chinese government provides aid for the reinauguration of the Lembá Tribunal in São Tomé and Príncipe
column9: On March 29, 2021, the ceremony of the reinauguration of the Lembá Tribunal was held. The newly renovated building has a court room, offices for judges and judicial police, two cells, and a nursery for minors. According to a Facebook post uploaded by the São Tomé and Príncipe Department of Justice, the renovation of the building cost 1.8 million dobras. The funding for the building was provided by the Government of China.

column8: Chinese People's Liberation Army's medical team donated medical equipments worth 0.5M RMB to the Laos 103 Military Hospital. (linked to #65324)
column9: From July 25 to August 8, 2017, the Chinese People's Liberation Army dispatched 90 personnels to carry out free medical service in Luang Namtha Province and Vientiane in Laos (or 中国人民解放军 “和平列车—2017”医疗服务队"). During the visit, the team donated more than 2000 pieces of medical equipments including medicines, training protective gear, etc., with a total value of 500000 RMB, to the Laos 103 military hospital._x000D_ _x000D_ It is linked to #65324, the medical support from the team.

column8: People's Liberation Army donates medications and medical equipment worth RMB 500,000 (Linked to Project ID#88686 and #88757)
column9: In August 2019, the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) provided medical assistance to Laos under Peace Train-2019 (see linked project ID#88686). As part of the assistance, a PLA medical team traveled to the Hospital of the 5th Division of the Lao People's Armed Forces in Pakse City in the Champasak Province. The team arrived on August 23, 2019. It brought medications and medical equipment worth RMB 500,000, which it was set to donate to Laos after the completion of the medical assistance. Further details are unknown.

column8: China donates motorcycles and office equipment worth 37 million CFA in 2015
column9: On May 7, 2015, China handed over the donation of motorcycles, LED screens, computers, photocopiers, and fax machines to Togo. Chinse Ambassador to Togo, Liu Yuxi, and the Togolese Minister of Foreign Affairs, Robert Dussey attended the donation ceremony. The equipment was estimated to be worth 37 million CFA and was donated in preparation for the upcoming African Union Summit on Maritime Security and Development.

column8: The Chinese Consulate General in Kuching donates 201,000 masks to the Sarawak State Disaster Management Committee in June 2021 (linked to project ID #96940, #96942)
column9: In June 2021, the Chinese Consulate General in Kuching donated 201,000 masks to the Sarawak State Disaster Management Committee (a total of 67 boxes) to support medical workers and other front-line anti-epidemic personnel. Minister of Local Government and Housing of Sarawak Dato' Seri Sim Kwai Hsien received supplies on behalf of the Sarawak Disaster Management Committee.   This was part of a series of donations to various entities in Sarawak State, Malaysia, in June 2021. Other donations include 99,000 masks (30 boxes) to the Federation of Sarawak Chinese Associations (see project ID #96940) and a total of 380,000 masks to the Immigration Bureau, Police Station, Fire and Rescue Bureau, charity organizations and other sectors of Sarawak (see project ID #96942).

column8: China donates 1000 motocycles to Indonesian police force
column9: In September 2003, China donated 1000 Chinese-made motorcycles to the Indonesia police. The motorcycles, which are equipped with sirens and radio receivers, were handed over by Chinese Ambassador to Indonesia Lu Shumin to Police Chief General Da'i Bachtiar. The valuation of the donation was at $1 million.

column8: Chinese municipality of Lishui donated medical supplies to Municipality of Santiago and Police in Chile April 2020
column9: On April 6th 2020, the Chinese municipality of Lishui donated medical supplies worth an estimated $44,000 to the Municipality of Santiago and Police in Chile. Specifically, Lishui donated 60,000 masks to the Municipality of Santiago. Lishui also donated 40,000 masks and 15,000 pairs of surgical gloves to Police stations in China. The purpose of this donation is to assist Chile in fighting against the pandemic.

column8: China National Offshore Oil Corporation provides GYD $10 million grant to Guyana's Civil Defense Commission for flood relief efforts
column9: On June 9, 2021, China National Offshore Oil Corporation donated GYD $10 million to the Civil Defense Commission in Guyana. The purpose of this donation was to aid flood relief efforts throughout the country.

column8: Chinese Government donates thermometers and face masks to Sri Lanka's Ministry of Defence in April 2020
column9: On April 8, 2020, the Chinese Government donated 70 frontal thermometers, 750 medical disposable 20-mask packets (15,000 masks), 2,080 medical disposal 10-mask packets (20,800 masks), 440 medical disposable 50-mask packets (22,000 masks) to Sri Lanka's Ministry of Defence.

column8: China donates 1st shipment of anti-epidemic materials to Venezuela in March 2020
column9: On March 19, 2020, the first shipment of anti-epidemic materials from China arrived in Venezuela. The shipment included 4,000 early diagnosis test kits, as well as materials used to administer these tests such as biosecurity suits, protective goggles, gloves, and air purifiers to support Venezuelan health care systems. The shipment arrived at Simon Bolivar International Airport in Caracas.

column7: Trinidad and Tobago Ministry of National Security
column8: Chinese government donates natural disaster equipment to National Security Ministry
column9: On April 28, 2023, the Chinese government donated 30 emergency tents, 10 standby generators, 5 rescue boats with of engines, fuel containers, and 25 life jackets to Trinidad and Tobago's Office of Disaster Preparedness and Management, a division of the National Security Ministry. The donation was completed at a handover ceremony held on April 28, 2023. Later, in November 2023, the materials were disbursed by the Office of Disaster Preparedness and Management to various government bodies, including the Ministry of Rural Development and Local Government’s Disaster Management Units, the Trinidad and Tobago Defense Force, the Trinidad and Tobago Police Force, the Trinidad and Tobago Fire Service, and the Tobago Emergency Management Agency. The donation was valued at TT $330,000.00.

column8: Chinese embassy donates 10 motorcycles to Sierra Leone Police Headquarters in 2022
column9: On June 14, 2022, the Chinese Embassy in Sierra Leone donated 10 motorcycles to the Sierra Leone Police headquarters. The donation was made to help improve transportation conditions in remote areas. The donation is valued at roughly $43473.12.

column8: The Chinese Consulate General in Kuching donates 99,000 masks to the Federation of Sarawak Chinese Associations in June 2021 (linked to project #96941, #96942)
column9: In June 2021, the Chinese Consulate General in Kuching donated 99,000 masks, or a total of thirty boxes, to the Federation of Sarawak Chinese Associations. Consul General Cheng Guangzhong led the staff of the Consulate General to donate masks to the Federation of Sarawak Chinese Associations.  This was part of a series of donations to various entities in Sarawak State, Malaysia, in June 2021. Other donations include 201,000 masks (67 boxes) to the Sarawak State Disaster Management Committee (see project ID #96941) and a total of 380,000 masks to the Immigration Bureau, Police Station, Fire and Rescue Bureau, charity organizations, and other sectors of Sarawak (see project ID #96942).

column8: People's Liberation Army donates medical protective gear to the South African National Defense Force (SANDF) in November 2020 (linked to project ID#93500 and 93502)
column9: On November 27, 2020, the People's Liberation Army donated medical protective gear to the South African National Defense Force (SANDF). The supplies included 30,000 masks, 400 suits, and 500 thermometers. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.   The supplies were donated in a handover ceremony where Rear Admiral Bravo Mhlana received the donation on behalf of SANDF.  The donation of medical supplies to SANDF was a part of a series of medical supply donations on behalf of the People's Liberation Army of China; previous donations occurred in March 2020 (project ID#93500) and August 2020 (project ID#93502).

column8: Chinese Embassy in Malawi donates motorcycles worth K20 million to police
column9: On June 16, 2017, the Chinese embassy donated motorcycles to the Malawian police, according to the Chinese Embassy. According to the Malawi Times, 14 motorcycles were donated at a value of K20 million.  Around 100 people attended the ceremony, including Ambassador Wang, the Minister of the Interior and Internal Security, Chiumia, The Secretary-General of the State, Madura, and police chief Kachama, among other government officials and police officers.

column8: Chinese Embassy in Benin donates 45 motorcycles to the Republican Police of Benin
column9: On September 8, 2022, the Chinese Embassy in Benin provided 45 motorbikes to the Republican Police of Benin. The total value of the bikes came in at 20 million West African CFA francs. The purpose of the donation was to ameliorate the operational capacity of the Police.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation. Peng Jingtao, China’s Ambassador to Benin, and Sai Yidu, Minister of the Interior and Public Security of Benin, attended the ceremony and delivered speeches. The Secretary-General of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, the main heads of ministries and commissions, and the main heads of the Republic Police also attended.

column8: Chinese Government donates printers, laptops, TVs and other equipment valued at Rs. 675,000 to the Mauritius Police Force
column9: In 2012, the Chinese Government donated 15 system unit Lenovos, 15 flat panel monitor Lenovos, 10 HP Printers, 5 Lenovo laptops, 2 LCD Hisense TVs and 1 Konika TV to the Mauritius Police Force. These items have an estimated value of 675,000 Rs. The donation was received on June 5, 2012.

column8: China Embassy grants two segways to Royal Barbados Police Force
column9: On February 28, 2018, the Chinese ambassador to Barbados handed over two segways, valued at BDS$40,000, to the Royal Barbados Police Force (RBPF). The handover occurred at RBPF headquarters, and the Embassy Political Counsellor Zou Xi, Barbadian Chief Inspector Tyrone Griffins as well as all assistant chief inspectors attended the ceremony. The grant is intended to improve the response time of the police force.

column8: Chinese government grants 2,560,000 Jamaican dollars to the National Police College of Jamaica to improve Chinese language training classes
column9: On 18 November 2018, the Ambassador of the People's Republic of China to Jamaica, Tian Qi, donated 2,560,000 Jamaican dollars to the Chinese language classes at the National Police College of Jamaica (NPCJ). The donation will be used to improve the Chinese language classroom and to attract more police officers to learn Chinese language, culture, and history. The donation follows the 2017 establishment of a Mandarin program at the college.

column8: China donates FCFA 10 million worth of Agricultural tools and Office Equipment to Ex-Servicemen and War Victims in Cameroon
column9: On April 25th, 2017, Chinese Ambassador to Cameroon handed over agricultural tools and office equipment to Ex-Servicemen and War Victims in Cameroon. This donation was given to Cameroon's Secretary of State in the Ministry of Defense in charge of Ex-Servicemen and War Victims, Koumpa Issa, from the Chinese Ambassador to Cameroon, Wei Wenhua. The materials comprising of cutlasses, hoes, sprayers, watering cans, rain boats, wheel barrows, trucks, dig axe, artisanal oil milling machine, six computers and two printers are worth FCFA 10 million. This project is completed._x000D_ _x000D_

column8: Chinese Government donates fans and air conditioners to Guinea Ministry of Security and Emergency Preparedness
column9: On January 1, 2015, the Ambassador of China in Guinea, Bian Jianqiang, presented a donation of equipment and facilities to the Guinean Ministry of Security and Emergency Preparedness. This donation was worth 120 million Guinean francs (16,000 USD) and included 25 air conditioners and 25 fans.

column8: 20th Chinese peacekeeping force donates medicine worth USD 22,000 to a Lebanese village in November 2021 (Linked to Record ID#94431)
column9: On November 29, 2021, the 20th Chinese peacekeeping force dispatched to Lebanon provided medicine, worth USD 22,000, to a local village in Nabatieh, South Lebanon. The force donated 51 medications, including antihypertensive, antibacterial, and topical drugs, as well as analgesics. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.  The donation occurred in a handover ceremony attended by Chinese Liaison officer Duan Da and the head of the Lebanese village.

column8: China Ministry of State Security donates masks to Ukraine in April 2020
column9: On April 10, 2020, 20,000 three-layer medical masks and 1,000 N95 masks donated by China's Ministry of State Security were held in a warehouse in Beijing to be loaded onto a plane to Ukraine. The supplies were eventually delivered to Ukraine.

column8: Chinese Government provides grant worth EGP 55,000 provision of computers and fax machines to Egypt's Ministry of Defense Language Institute
column9: On November 5, 2008, according to Egyptian Ministry of Defense and Military Production Resolution No. 132 of 2008, the Government Egypt accepted a grant of eight computers and two fax machines worth EGP 55,000 pounds from the Chinese Government for the Ministry of Defense Language Institute (also known as Languages ​​Armed Forces Institute or معهد لغات القوات المسلحة). The specific Chinese Government institution that donated the materials is unknown.

column8: China grants computer packages worth 20,000 kina to Papua New Guinea police
column9: On May 17, 2001, five computer packages worth more than 20,000 kina were donated to the Royal Papua New Guinea Police Constabulary. The computers were donated by the Chinese government and received by Police Minister Jimson Sauk in Port Moresby. They included printers, inkjets, diskettes and other computer accessories. Mr Sauk said three of the computers would be used at police headquarters at Konedobu while the other two would be used in the ministry. The computers will greatly benefit the entire constabulary and the ministry in their effort to effectively compile and store vital information in their job as law enforcers.  Mr Zhao Zhenyu said the government would give more computers later in the year.

column8: Chinese government donates 7.5 million colons in supplies to Costa Rican Ministry of Public Security
column9: On or about December 1, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Costa Rica handed over a donation of supplies worth 7.5 million colons to Costa Rica's Ministry of Public Security to be used by police forces in the country, particularly those patrolling the border.  More specifically, the donation included 164 pairs of steel-toed rubber boots, a canopy that will serve as a food and meeting center measuring 8x8 meters, 240 units of sunscreen, and 25,000 disposable masks.

column8: Embassy of China in Myanmar donates police bicycles and communication equipment to the Yangon Provincial Police Department in 2017
column9: On January 13, 2017, based on the press release from Embassy of China in Myanmar, the Embassy donates 100 police bicycles and 13 intercoms to the Yangon Provincial Police Department. According to the release from CRI.cn, the value of the donation is about USD 12 thousand._x000D_

column8: Chinese Government provides 10,000 surgical masks to Argentina in June 2020
column9: On June 12, 2020, the Chinese government made a donation of 10,000 surgical masks to the Governor of the Jujuy province in Argentina and the Minister of Security. The masks will be dispersed throughout the different sectors in Jujuy that need them the most.   The donation was part of the "Jujuy Seguro e Interconectado" (Safe and Interconnected Jujuy) Project.

column7: Dar es Salaam Special Zone Police
column8: Changzhou City Police Bureau Donates Laptops to Tanzanian Police
column9: On November 24, 2012, the Police Bureau of Changzhou City donated ten laptops to the Dar es Salaam Special Zone Police for facilitation of combating crime. The donation was worth an estimated 15 million Tanzanian shillings.

column7: Lesotho Ministry of Police and Public Safety
column8: China donates 100,000 M for greenhouse project at the Police Training College in Lesotho
column9: On November 27, 2018, the Chinese Ambassador, Mr. Song Changqing, officially handed over a 100,000 M check to the Police Training College (PTC) in Lesotho to assist in a greenhouse project. In the same donation ceremony, China also donated community policing kit and resources, including blankets, gumboots and torches, to the Lesotho Ministry of Police and Public Safety (Project ID#55767). Furthermore, China has also agreed to donating a fingerprint examination lab to Lesotho.

column8: Chinese government provides masks to Mayor's Office of Panama City in April 2020
column9: On April 8, 2020, the Chinese government donated 10,000 masks to the Mayor’s Office of Panama City. These masks will be utilized by staff and working personnel of the office. They will be distributed among collaborators of the Municipality of Panama, the Houses of Peace, and the Municipal Police. The monetary value of this donation is unknown. Mayor José Luis Fábrega accepted this donation which was handed over by the Chinese Embassy.

column8: Chinese Embassy in Sri Lanka donates materials valued 1.5 million rupees to the Seva Vanitha Unit of the Sri Lanka Air Force in November 2021
column9: On November 12, 2021, the Embassy of China made a donation of over Rs. 1.5 million to the Seva Vanitha Unit of the Sri Lanka Air Force. This was delivered by the Chinese delegation led by the Defence Attache of the Chinese Embassy in Sri Lanka, Senior Colonel Wan Dong. The purpose of this donation is to continue the dedicated work by the SLAF Seva Vanitha Unit to uplift the living standards of families of service and civilian personnel who are in need through welfare projects in the year 2022.

column8: Colombo International Container Terminals contributes to a donation of three wheelchairs worth $9,000 USD to wheelchair tennis players (Linked to Project ID#95354)

column8: Chinese government donates face masks and shields to the Philippines
column9: On October 30, 2020, the Chinese government, through its Ministry of Public Security (MPS), donated over 40 boxes of face masks and face shields to the Bureau of Customs (BOC). The donation from the MPS of the People's Republic of China was received by Commissioner Rey Leonardo Guerrero together with Deputy Commissioner for Intelligence Group (IG) Raniel Ramiro, during the turnover ceremony on Friday at the OCOM Conference Room, Port of Manila, the BOC said in a statement. According to the BOC, this batch of medical supplies consisting of 20 boxes of face masks and 22 boxes of face shields, the personal protective equipment shall be used in ensuring the safety and health of the men and women of the Bureau in the delivery of efficient public service.

column8: Chinese Government donates 200 motorcycles to the Trinidad and Tobago Police Service
column9: On August 21, 2019, Chinese ambassador Song Yumin formally presented a gift of 200 motorcycles to the Trinidad and Tobago Police Service (TTPS) at the Policy Academy in St. James, Port of Spain. The course was hosted by the Chinese Ministry of Public Security and was jointly organized by Chongqing Police Academy and the Trinidad and Tobago Police Academy. 30 officers from various branches of the Special Police Force and immigration border inspection participated in the training, which covered forensic inspection in the fields of technology, homicide investigation office, DNA inspection technology, criminal image processing, and drug inspection. column8: Chinese Embassy donates 12 motorcycles to the Tonga-China Friendship Association

column8: Chinese naval hospital ship Ark Peace arrived at Tonga to provide medical service (linked to project #37762)
column9: On 13 August, 2018, the Chinese naval hospital ship Ark Peace arrived at Port Nukualofa, capital of the Kingdom of Tonga, the fourth stop of Mission Harmony 2018, starting an eight-day good-will visit and humanitarian medical service. Ark Peace paid her first successful visit to Tonga on the same date four years ago. (See project #37762)_x000D_ The Tongan government hosted a grand welcome ceremony at the Vuna Wharf. At the ceremony, the Acting Prime Minister Sika warmly welcomed Ark Peace's second visit to Tonga on behalf of the Tongan government and conveyed his appreciation to the ship for providing medical services to the Tongan people. _x000D_ Ambassador Wang pointed out that the second visit of Ark Peace, as an important part of events to jointly celebrate the 20th anniversary of the normalization of relations between China and Tonga, will further strengthen mutual trust and friendship between the two countries and the two armed forces.

column8: China military hospital ship provides medical services to Tonga (linked to project #65343)
column9: On August 13, the Peace Ark hospital ship of the Chinese People’s Liberation Army Navy arrived at the port of Nukualofa, Vuna Wharf in Tonga for a 7-day visit. While providing various medical services, the hospital ship also sent its medical team to local hospitals to carry out surgical operations in cooperation with the medical staff of Tonga, and set up medical teams to pay rounds of visits to remote islands and islets to provide diagnosis and treatment services. In addition, it also sent its teams to local schools and centers for the disabled to give diagnosis and treatment and carry out donation activities. The ship departed on Wednesday, 20 August after a week of providing free medical services that included 39 surgeries, including removing a bullet from a Tongan who had been shot while he was in the United States. Medical teams were also dispatched to the Vaiola Hospital. Patients on ‘Eua Island also received free assistance when a team flew to the island on board the vessel’s medical helicopter._x000D_

column8: 16th Chinese Deployment of Police Forces in Timor-Leste
column9: On May 11, 2011, China sent its 16th deployment of peacekeeping forces to Timor Leste. This squad comprised of 23 members from the Department of Public Safety of Fujian Province. Member had received training from the Chinese Peacekeeping Police Training Center in topics such as situation identification, international law and peacekeeping behaviors. They will replace the 15th deployment from Shandong Province and will complete a year long mission in Timor Leste with the United Nations. The 16th batch of Chinese peacekeepers would return to China at the end of 2012.

The team formally began their work on May 22, 2012 and returned to China November of the same year. Prior to their tenure, the team underwent nine months of training in preparation for their mission.

column9: China sent its 15th deployment of peacekeeping police officers to Timor-Leste May 11, 2010. The team comprised of 24 members from the province of Shandong with backgrounds in criminal investigation, public security, and traffic control. Like previous teams, the Chinese police officers will be working with the UN mission in Timor-Leste to help stabilize the country. Eight out of the 24 police personnel had previously participated in United Nations peacekeeping missions.

column8: Chinese Government provides training for teachers from Zimbabwe Wushu Association (ZWA)
column9: In February 2013, China sent Wushu experts to train 63 local teachers in this form of martial arts at Chaminuka Training Centre in Mashonaland Central province. In August 2013, China was to select the top twenty teachers from the local school to travel to China and enhance their skills in Wushu martial arts. The selected teachers were to stay in China for one year.  The teachers arrived in China in November 2013 to study at Tianjin Huo Yuanjia Civil and Military School for African students. According to China Daily, the Zimbabwean students ended up studying Chinese more than Yushu. Zimbabwean Deputy Minister Dokora said the move to send the teachers to China reflected the good ties that the two countries enjoyed. “This is reciprocal and they too will be benefiting from English classes given by the Zimbabwe nationals,” he said. He said the program was being implemented in fulfillment of the China–Africa cooperation framework.  The ZWA president, Gilbert Makowah, said the Chinese Ambassador would also look at the prospects of getting some scholarships for Zimbabwean Wushu fighters. This training comes as a result of an agreement signed on 2 January, 2012, where the Chinese Embassy in Harare pledged development support for the Zimbabwe Wushu Association (ZWA).

column8: Chinese Government donation of office equipment to the police force in Myanmar in 2012

He said that the Myanmar police are willing to further strengthen law enforcement cooperation between the two countries._x000D_

column8: Chinese Government donates 180 solar water heaters to Zimbabwe Republic Police (ZRP) in 2006
column9: On August 24, 2006, the Chinese Government donated 180 solar water heaters to the Zimbabwe Republic Police as part of a project to introduce China's experience and technology in solar energy development to the solar energy-rich country.  The goal of this project was to evaluate the performance of the Chinese-made solar heaters under local conditions, to train local technicians in installation and maintenance, to demonstrate the green energy technology, and to promote commercial and industrial cooperation in green energy.  The pilot project, worth 1.5 million yuan (187,500 U.S. dollars), was completed in 1998, positively affecting the lives of 110 households.  The financial value of this second phase of the project is unclear.

column9: On May 22, 2014, China’s Ministry of Commerce sent a team to assist in the design and training of a choreography team for Zambia’s 50th Independence Day celebration (or “Golden Jubilee Celebration”) on October 24, 2014. column8: 18th military medical team dispatched to Zambia
column9: China has been sending military medical teams to Zambia since 1984. On January 20, 2015, China’s 18th military medical team arrived in Zambia. They also provided medical care for the President and the First Lady, and treated hundreds of senior officials and officers from both Zambian government and military.
